results.title: To watch and watch for: Week of Nov. 1
results.description: After a surely productive Halloweekend and the conclusion of Hoptoberfest always comes the onset of November and an imminent Thanksgiving. It is in between the spooky and the cuffing season that we find the rest of the genres neatly lined up for us to enjoy with friends and perhaps a dinner party to follow. If you're looking for an excuse to find reprieve from studying, a cozy JHMI read or an album to put on while getting ready in the morning, make sure to give this week's picks a chance! After premiering at the Venice International Film Festival this past September, the dark comedy spy thriller Wild Horse Nine is receiving its theatrical release this week. The film follows CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) on their deployment to Easter Island shortly before the military coup that would install Pinochet as President. As they uncover more details about their past and present situations, things seem to keep throwing their plans sideways. The movie is both deeply pensive and hilariously funny with a notable standout performance to watch for from Malkovich, who received Best Actor at Venice for his role. With the NBA season's recent tipoff, talks about greatness, potential and unfortunately, injuries have already taken off in full force. Even with all of the talent on display in the modern league, players and fans alike must always remember the giants whose shoulders the present game of basketball stands on, and the legendary coach Phil Jackson won't let us forget that. In the book Masters of the Game, close friends Jackson and former sports journalist Sam Smith discuss the stories of the all-time best players and the details that make up basketball history, both on and off the court. Unfortunately for fans of Bearface's contemplative parts on songs like SUMMER, the singer has kept his head down since BROCKHAMPTON's breakup in 2022. However, this July, he released K-Bar under the name Ciarán and has since been teasing songs from his upcoming album Róisín ever since. For fans looking for introspective alternative RnB and brilliantly harmonized falsettos, this long-awaited return might be just the release to scratch your brain. Too often, music listeners are allowed to see music as a solitary act. Streaming services allow us to pipe music directly into our own ears and allow us to forget what recommending your favorite to your friends was like. Artist in Residence Xavier "Seven" Walker is combating this by presenting the Black album Frequency Sound Library, a listening room focused on community building and growing roots in the sounds of Baltimore. Pop by on Nov. 5 to join in on the process of cultural creation! As always, you can also check out the extended list below for even more recommendations!
